purpose: V-004 GroupCommitOrdering model (GroupCommit.tla): every config and its expected TLC outcome. A violation expecting '<temporal>' is a failed liveness/convergence property; its counterexample is a mutation regression vector.

models.claim: ADR-0173: with a faulty (offline, censoring or equivocating) coordinator, racing direct reductions, non-reducing coordinator commits and replacements, every honest member converges on one canonical chain, forked members rejoin or stay out, and every reducing intent is applied or moot; no honest author equivocates; the coordinator never sequences its own removal or replacement
ADR-0173: the same races with no faulty member converge
ADR-0128 rule 1: a member removes an offline coordinator directly and the succession replaces it deterministically
mutation: an order key without the reducing-first class lets a coordinator's non-reducing commit outrank a reduction at the same parent
mutation: a member that does not detect that its merged commit lost stays active on a non-canonical chain (silent key/state continuation)
mutation: fork recovery without the roster check re-adds a device that the canonical chain removed
mutation: a restart that forgets the prepared commit lets an honest author publish a second, different commit at the same parent (ADR-0163 rules 2, 3, 9)
mutation: the coordinator may sequence its own removal
